lessons.title: Diminutives: -tjie, -ie, -jie
explanation: Afrikaans speakers love making words "little" — for size, cuteness, or friendliness.
**-ie** after most consonants: boek → **boekie**, kop → **koppie** (also: cup).
**-tjie** after a long vowel and after -l, -n, -r: tafel → **tafeltjie**, deur → **deurtjie**. After a short vowel the consonant doubles: man → **mannetjie**.

exercises.en: A small dog is a little dog.
A small tree is a little tree.
A small table is a little table.

lessons.title: Adjectives before nouns
explanation: Some adjectives add **-e** before a noun: **Die huis is groot** but **'n groot huis** (no change), while **Die man is vriendelik** → **'n vriendelike man**.
Long adjectives (-ig, -lik) usually add -e: **'n lelike hond**. Short common ones often don't: **'n groot huis**, **'n mooi meisie**, **'n klein kind**.
Some change shape: **oud → ou** (die ou man), **nuut → nuwe** (die nuwe kar), **jonk → jong**, **lank → lang**.
Comparing: **groot → groter → grootste**, **mooi → mooier → mooiste**, **goed → beter → beste**.

examples.af: Die ou man is baie vriendelik.
examples.en: The old man is very friendly.

examples.af: My broer is groter as ek.
examples.en: My brother is bigger than me.

exercises.en: The old man is my grandpa.
My brother is bigger than me.
